region: Panorama Route, Kruger, Zululand and the Drakensberg
title: South Africa — Escarpment, Lowveld Bush and the Amphitheatre Wall
subtitle: A 15-day self-drive loop from Johannesburg through the Panorama Route, Kruger, Zululand and the Drakensberg
summary: A loop from Johannesburg through the Panorama Route and two camping nights in Kruger, then rhino and hippo country in Zululand and a Tugela Falls hike and San rock art in the uKhahlamba-Drakensberg.
introduction: The trip starts with two history stops in Johannesburg, the Apartheid Museum and Constitution Hill, then a rental SUV climbs the Mpumalanga escarpment to Graskop for God's Window and the Blyde River Canyon. Two nights camping at Skukuza and Lower Sabie in Kruger lead to a long road south to Zululand: rhino in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi, hippos in the St Lucia estuary and the beach at Cape Vidal. The final week climbs to the Amphitheatre rim for the Tugela Falls and walks to San rock paintings at Giant's Castle, in the UNESCO-listed Drakensberg. About 3,200 km, sealed roads almost throughout, no night driving.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is arid wadis and forts. This route is green-season Lowveld bush, Indian Ocean wetlands and basalt escarpment, with wildlife and apartheid history instead of Arabian fort and desert camping culture.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: A package would fly into Kruger lodges and a Durban beach. This plan drives itself through four protected-area systems, camps in SANParks and Ezemvelo sites and spends a day on the Amphitheatre rim.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Complements D17 (Cape rock art and Karoo passes) with the other half of South Africa; no other portfolio route pairs self-drive Big Five bush, hippo estuaries and a World Heritage mountain hike with the apartheid story.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound overnight flight (arrive day 2); day 14 return overnight flight (arrive day 15).

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Slightly less rain and cloud than February, cooler nights in the mountains, and the window ends before the Human Rights Day long weekend (Sunday 21 March, Monday 22 March observed). Kruger Lower Sabie campsite rates are lower until 18 March (R488 versus R552, S10).

februarySuitability.summary: Hot and humid Lowveld and coast with frequent afternoon thunderstorms; cyclone-driven rain can flood roads in the Lowveld and KwaZulu-Natal; Kruger vegetation is at its densest; malaria season. Still workable with early starts.

marchSuitability.summary: Rain and cloud ease slightly, Drakensberg mornings are clearer and nights cooler, and Kruger camp rates are lower until 18 March; storms and malaria season persist. Better of the two months.

climate.regionNote: Approximate normals for Johannesburg, Skukuza/Lowveld, St Lucia coast and Drakensberg foothills; recalled typical values and the climate overview, not a 2027 forecast.

february.rainfall: Summer-rainfall peak: roughly 100-150 mm in the Lowveld, coast and Drakensberg; heavy afternoon thunderstorms.
february.humidity: High in the Lowveld and on the coast.
february.notes: Cyclone remnants from the Mozambique Channel can bring flooding. Johannesburg about 26/16, Skukuza about 32/20, St Lucia about 29/22, foothills about 25/14 (approximate).

march.rainfall: Rain easing: roughly 60-110 mm; storms still frequent but fewer.
march.humidity: High, easing late in the month.
march.notes: Johannesburg about 24/14, Skukuza about 30/19, St Lucia about 28/21, foothills about 23/12 (approximate); colder above 2,500 m.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow in summer; storms, lightning and mist are the hazard on the Amphitheatre rim and chain ladders; some Drakensberg gravel roads close after heavy rain; Sani Pass is often closed in bad weather (S16).
climate.seaConditions: Indian Ocean is warm at Cape Vidal; strong currents, swim only where patrolled; hippos and crocodiles in estuaries.
climate.airQuality: Good in the escarpment and mountains; hazy in Gauteng.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Green season: animals dispersed and bush dense, so Kruger sightings are harder than in the dry season, but birds and young animals are abundant. Rhino remain visible in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Human Rights Day
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Long-weekend road traffic and fatal-accident peak (FCDO notes weekends and public holidays); the window avoids it.

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: no closures expected on this route.
climate.tourismDemand: Low to moderate: after the December-January peak and before the Easter school holidays; Kruger camps book out on weekends.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Shoulder season for CDG-JNB after the December peak; early-March fares are typically below peak. Not verified.

geography.summary: From the Highveld across the Drakensberg escarpment into the Lowveld, then the Zululand coastal plain and back up to the high Drakensberg.
geography.distinctive: Within one loop: the Blyde River Canyon rim, Africa's oldest reserve (1895), a World Heritage estuary where hippos walk the streets and a 948 m waterfall on the Amphitheatre wall.

signatureExperiences.title: Panorama Route at dawn
signatureExperiences.description: God's Window, Bourke's Luck Potholes and the Three Rondavels on a one-day loop from Graskop.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The escarpment is the scale of the Blyde River Canyon, and dawn light and mist change the views each hour.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Stay two nights in Graskop and start at God's Window at opening; pay entry at gates.

signatureExperiences.title: Camping on the Sabie River in Kruger
signatureExperiences.description: Self-drive the Skukuza to Lower Sabie river road and camp in rest camps.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Hippo and elephant at the river from your own vehicle, with a campsite braai instead of a lodge.
signatureExperiences.location: Skukuza and Lower Sabie, Kruger National Park
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book SANParks campsites months ahead; conservation fee R692 per adult per day; use Phabeni Gate only.
signatureExperiences.costNote: 3 days of conservation fees plus campsites.

signatureExperiences.title: Rhino and hippo country in Zululand
signatureExperiences.description: Self-drive Hluhluwe-iMfolozi, then a boat on the St Lucia estuary.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Africa's oldest reserve (1895) with one of the largest white rhino populations, then hippos from the water.
signatureExperiences.location: Hluhluwe-iMfolozi Park and iSimangaliso Wetland Park
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book Ezemvelo accommodation; book the estuary cruise on arrival.

signatureExperiences.title: Tugela Falls from the Amphitheatre rim
signatureExperiences.description: Guided hike from the Sentinel car park up the chain ladders to the plateau and falls.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The route reaches the top of a 948 m, five-stage waterfall and an Amphitheatre wall about 5 km long.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hire a licensed local guide; start at dawn; fall back to the Tugela Gorge walk in storms.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Guide about R1,000 per group, shared.

signatureExperiences.title: San rock art at Giant's Castle
signatureExperiences.description: Guided walk to the Main Caves.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Original paintings in a World Heritage shelter with a guide to the stories.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book the Main Caves tour with Ezemvelo when booking the chalet.

travelStyle.summary: A 3,200 km self-drive loop mixing rest-camp camping with guesthouses and reserve chalets; two licence holders alternate.

transport.summary: Rental from OR Tambo on arrival; return there. Roads are sealed and busy; fuel is available in all towns.

modes.description: Fortuner or Hilux class for four adults and camping gear; 4x4 not needed except for Sani Pass.
St Lucia estuary hippo cruise on day 9.

transport.carRental: JNB has the major international and local rental firms. Enterprise lists a minimum age of 23, no additional drivers on cross-border rentals and R2,500 per border; one-way fees show only at booking (S19). The loop avoids one-way fees; a Durban drop-off is possible but not planned. Cross-border to Eswatini or Lesotho needs 72 h notice and written authorisation.

drivingRequirements.summary: Left-hand drive, sealed roads, no night driving; main hazards are crime, trucks and weekend traffic.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: An English-language licence with photo and signature is generally accepted; for a French licence carry an IDP as a safeguard; rental terms not verified today.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two travellers hold car licences and both are named on the rental; the other two are passengers.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycles; use car passenger seats, ride-hailing or guided tours.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Alternate the two drivers on long days (7, 11, 14), never drive after dark, keep the tank above half, never cross protester roadblocks, stop only in busy places.

accommodation.summary: Rest-camp campsites in Kruger and Royal Natal, guesthouses in Johannesburg, Graskop, Pongola and St Lucia, and Ezemvelo chalets or huts at Hluhluwe-iMfolozi and Giant's Castle.

camping.summary: Four nights camping (Skukuza, Lower Sabie, Mahai x2) with hired tents; other nights indoors for weather and recovery. Use fenced rest-camp sites only: hippo and hyena roam outside.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Mostly driving with short walks, but the Tugela Falls day is 6-8 h on steep ground with chain ladders, and long drives on days 7, 11 and 14.

itinerary.summary: Day 1 flight, day 2 Johannesburg history, days 3-4 Panorama Route, days 5-7 Kruger and the road to Zululand, days 8-10 Hluhluwe-iMfolozi, St Lucia and Cape Vidal, days 11-14 Drakensberg and return, day 15 arrival in Paris.

days.title: Overnight flight south
activities: Evening departure Saturday 6 March, overnight flight
days.practical: Book a daytime arrival at JNB; France Diplomatie reports armed robberies of arriving travellers.

days.title: Rental car and the Apartheid Museum
activities: Morning arrival, collect rental car in daylight
Early night at a guarded guesthouse
days.practical: Do not use ATMs or exchange at the airport; plan the route before leaving; keep windows up and doors locked.

days.title: Highveld to the escarpment
activities: Leave about 07:30 on the N4 and N12
days.practical: Fuel before leaving the N4; arrive before dark; tolls on the N4.

days.title: Panorama Route
activities: Three Rondavels viewpoint and Blyde River Canyon
Lisbon Falls on the way back
days.geographicalHighlight: Blyde River Canyon, God's Window, potholes
days.practical: Start early: afternoon thunderstorms and mist are common in February and March; viewpoint entry fees in cash or card.

days.title: Into Kruger by Phabeni Gate
activities: Drive Graskop to Phabeni Gate via Hazyview in daylight
Self-drive afternoon on the Sabie River loop
days.practical: Avoid the R538 and Numbi Gate; do not stop on the roadside near Hazyview; check gate times (about 05:30 to 18:00 or 18:30); apply insect repellent, malaria risk area.

days.title: The Sabie River road
activities: Dawn drive along the Sabie River
Dusk drive and braai at Lower Sabie campsite
days.practical: Green season foliage hides animals; thunderstorms fill dry roads; no walking outside camps.

days.title: Long drive out of Kruger to Zululand
activities: Dawn drive, exit via Crocodile Bridge Gate
Drive via Malelane, Barberton and Piet Retief to Pongola
days.practical: The long driving day of the loop: alternate drivers; do not drive after dark; fuel above half; trucks on the N2 and fatal weekend traffic.

days.title: Rhino country
activities: Morning at Mkhuze Game Reserve hides
Self-drive and night at Hilltop or Mpila (chalet or hut)
days.travelTime: About 3 h 30 min plus game drives
days.practical: Book Ezemvelo accommodation; partly low-risk malaria area.

days.title: Hippos on the estuary
activities: Dawn drive in the Umfolozi section
Drive to St Lucia (1 h 45 min)
Hippos graze in town after dark: stay indoors
days.practical: Do not walk after dark in St Lucia.

days.title: Cape Vidal and the coast
activities: Drive the 30 km Cape Vidal road
Beach, reef-pool snorkelling and dune-forest walk
Spare day for weather, rest or a second cruise
days.geographicalHighlight: Dune forest, reef pools, Indian Ocean beach
days.practical: Hot and humid; storms can close the beach road; malaria precautions; swim only at patrolled spots.

days.title: Cross-country to the Drakensberg
activities: Leave at dawn via Mtubatuba, Vryheid and Ladysmith
Camp at Mahai below the Amphitheatre
days.practical: Longest drive of the trip: plan an early start and arrive before dark; take fuel in Ladysmith.

days.title: Tugela Falls from the Sentinel
activities: Leave at 05:30 for the Sentinel car park
Hike with a licensed guide to the chain ladders and the Amphitheatre rim
Walk to the Tugela Falls edge and return
If cloud or storms threaten: Tugela Gorge walk from Mahai instead
days.travelTime: About 1-1.5 h each way plus 6-8 h on foot
days.geographicalHighlight: Amphitheatre rim at about 3,000 m, Tugela Falls
days.practical: Turn back at the first thunder; carry rain gear, 3 L of water, a head torch; check the Sentinel road and Ezemvelo advisory before leaving.

days.title: San rock art
activities: Afternoon guided walk to the Main Caves
Night in a chalet at Giant's Castle
days.culturalHighlight: San rock art in the Main Caves, uKhahlamba-Drakensberg World Heritage Site
days.practical: Confirm the Main Caves tour time when booking.

days.title: Back to Johannesburg and the flight home
activities: Return the car in daylight and fly home that evening
days.practical: Allow a 2 h buffer for rental return and security at OR Tambo; the Human Rights Day long weekend begins Sunday 21 March, so leave on Friday 19 March.

stops.description: Beach reached by a 30 km road through dune forest, with snorkelling in the reef pools.

assumptions: Most 2026-27 park, accommodation and rental prices were not published in a source readable today; lines are labelled estimates.
Flights are a planning estimate, not a live quote.
Kruger conservation fee R692 per adult per day from 1 Nov 2026 comes from a news report; the SANParks PDF could not be read.
Loop route: no one-way fee, no cross-border fees.
unknownCosts: Royal Natal and Giant's Castle campsite and chalet rates
budget.exceptionalJustification: The realistic total of about EUR 2,380 per person is driven by park conservation fees (Kruger alone is R692 per adult per day), a 13-day rental for four adults and a EUR 780 return flight. It stays below EUR 2,500 and buys three distinct protected landscapes (escarpment, Lowveld bush and Zululand wetlands, UNESCO Drakensberg) plus the apartheid-history days. A credible cheaper variant is the economical scenario at about EUR 1,750 (compact SUV, more camping, unguided Tugela Gorge).

scenarioNotes.economical: Compact SUV, five camping nights, no guide (Tugela Gorge instead of the Sentinel route), minimal activities.
scenarioNotes.realistic: 7-seat SUV, four camping nights and eight room-nights, guided Sentinel route, one cruise and one guided drive.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: 4x4 with more lodge nights, extra guides and Kruger guided drives.

security.summary: No official source reviewed advises against any region on the route; the risk is ordinary violent and road crime, higher in Gauteng and on long KwaZulu-Natal drives than on the D17 Cape route, mitigated by daytime driving and fixed overnight stops.
security.assessedRoute: OR Tambo and Johannesburg, N4/N12 to Graskop, Panorama Route, Phabeni Gate to Skukuza and Lower Sabie, Crocodile Bridge, Malelane, Barberton, Piet Retief, Pongola, Mkhuze, Hluhluwe-iMfolozi, St Lucia, Cape Vidal, Ladysmith, Royal Natal, Giant's Castle, N3 to Johannesburg. Northern Kruger (Pafuri) and the Numbi Gate/R538 are excluded.

security.insuranceConsiderations: Cover medical, repatriation, hiking above 3,000 m, rental excess and theft; check chain-ladder hiking and wildlife exclusions.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; triggers: unrest or road blockades in Mpumalanga or KwaZulu-Natal, incidents at Phabeni, Crocodile Bridge or Malelane gates, cyclone or flood warnings, a change in French vigilance level, or protest-linked closures of the N2 or R538.

practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 30 days after departure and 2 blank pages (UK advice); confirm for the French passport.
